title: Valet
premise: The valet stand is at the edge of the sea. The ticket is number 12. There are no cars, there have never been cars, and a valet in a red jacket is already jogging into the surf with the fob held over his head.
visual: Overcast noon, wet sand, a proper brass-and-mahogany valet podium with a numbered key board — every hook full. A woman in sunglasses holds ticket 12 and waits with ordinary patience. Tyre tracks lead into the water and do not come back. Far out, a red jacket at chest height in the swell, arm up.
characterLean: Liliane will wait the full quarter hour out of politeness. Vivienne tips first and leaves.
notes: Seed only — still prompt not locked. Keep it flat overcast noon and completely ordinary in every other respect; sunset or night turns it into a dream sequence and the gag dies. The valet is professional, unhurried, and not drowning. Not the Pizza Guy — do not borrow his uniform or his persistence.
